chose: Added a rustfs-init one-shot to docker-compose.yml that chowns /data to the image's own rustfs uid before rustfs starts, wired via depends_on: service_completed_successfully
over: Deleting the buttery_s3 volume so rustfs recreates it with correct ownership
Renaming the volume so a service swap can never inherit the previous image's ownership
Running rustfs as user 0:0 to sidestep ownership entirely
because: Deleting or renaming fixes only this instance and loses the already-uploaded objects under buttery-uploads; the class returns for the next image that renumbers its user. Running as root diverges from the upstream image and would keep writing root-owned objects, re-arming the same trap. The init is idempotent, reuses the rustfs image so nothing extra is pulled, and reads the uid from the image passwd entry (id -u rustfs) rather than hardcoding 10001, so it self-heals across image changes. Verified: whole process-compose stack green, buttery-uploads/pending preserved.
